subject: health
title: Launch and diagnostic: assertive, respectful communication
essentialQuestion: How do I speak up for myself, respect others, and repair a relationship after conflict?
materials: paper or a digital tool for scripts
keyPoints: Passive gives in, aggressive attacks, assertive states your need and respects theirs.
A clear frame: "When ___ happens, I feel ___, and I would like ___." Tone, volume, and body language carry as much as the words.
Being assertive does not guarantee you get what you want; it makes being understood far more likely.
privacySafeScenario: A friend keeps borrowing things without asking. Write a passive, an aggressive, and an assertive version, and say why the third is better.
studentTask: The learner applies what they learned about assertive, respectful communication to a new fictional situation and records the choice plus the reason behind it.
knowledgeCheck: Name one thing you already knew about assertive, respectful communication and one question you now have.
completionCriteria: The learner completes the central task about assertive, respectful communication.
The learner gives a reason, an example, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name one next step.
adaptationChoices: Scripts may be spoken, signed, typed, drawn as a comic, or acted with figures. Role-play is optional and may always be replaced by describing what a character should say and why.
extensionChallenge: Apply what you learned about assertive, respectful communication under a new constraint, compare two reasonable approaches, or teach the idea to a family member with an original fictional example.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, signed, drawn, or pointed responses; the response mode is never the standard being assessed.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
trustedAdultNote: Direct urgent safety, health, or mental-health concerns to a trusted adult or qualified professional; this course is not diagnosis, therapy, or treatment.

optionalReflection.prompt: With a guardian, review who is on your list of adults you could tell if something felt wrong. This is optional. No purchase, account creation, photograph, measurement, or private disclosure is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
